title: Tenant-prioritized hotpatch lifecycle and cross-environment bridge playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and automation for performing tenant-prioritized hotpatches and coordinated rollbacks across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments during model rollout regressions or canary-quality failures. This work reduces time-to-fix for high-value tenants by enabling a short-circuit patch path: ephemeral model pinning, targeted traffic slices, preflight KV-cache validation, and a bridging procedure to align state between private networks and hosted control plane when live adjustments are required. The deliverable is a runnable runbook, a set of automation scripts (rehydrate + sweep), communication templates for support/SEs, and a small bridging service prototype to orchestrate cross-environment coordination when customers are running Private deployments with on-prem KV state or custom routing policies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A runnable runbook that an SRE or solutions engineer can execute in <30 minutes for a P0 tenant-impact regression
2) Automation script (rehydrate-sweep) that reconciles KV cache differences between a pinned model variant and fallback variant without requiring full tenant re-ingestion
3) Bridge service prototype that can register a Private deployment control-plane endpoint and perform a secure state-sync handshake (mutual TLS) with onboarding steps documented
4) Communication templates for customer-facing status updates and internal escalation that have been reviewed by Support and PM
5) End-to-end dry run performed on staging with telemetry demonstrating degraded canary detection -> hotpatch -> verification loop completes within SLA targets
6) Postmortem checklist and follow-up automation tasks created if manual steps were used during a live incident
steps: Preflight: Confirm canary metrics (response-quality, prompt-failure-rate, latency p95, embed-dist drift) on dashboard and tag affected tenants
Step 1 - Quarantine Slice: Create a temporary tenant slice in traffic router (slice-id) to divert only affected tenant(s) while keeping majority traffic on primary variant
Step 2 - Ephemeral Pin: Pin the affected tenant(s) to a stable model variant (ephemeral variant pin), update routing table, and set time-to-live for pin
Step 3 - KV-cache Preflight: Run 'rehydrate-check --tenant <id> --variant A --variant B' to surface missing prefix keys and estimated rehydrate cost

Step 4 - Rehydrate Sweep: If small delta, run 'rehydrate-sweep --tenant <id> --target-variant B --budget 1000-tokens' to populate KV cache for the pinned variant; otherwise schedule staged rehydrate with throttling

Step 5 - Bridge Sync (Private): If tenant is on Private/VPC, execute mutual-TLS handshake with the Private bridge endpoint using onboarding credentials and run 'bridge-sync --confirm-state --dry-run' before actual reconciliation

Step 6 - Canary Validation: Send golden prompts and customer repro cases to the pinned variant via test harness and verify outputs against regression thresholds; record artifacts to the incident folder
Step 7 - Customer Communication: Use template to send initial notification, status updates, and mitigation timeline; include mitigation artifacts and next-steps
Step 8 - Decide: If regression resolved, plan a staggered unpin and traffic reintroduction; if unresolved, prepare rollback to previous model image and follow rollback checklist
Step 9 - Post-incident: Run KV-cache cleanup, revoke ephemeral pins, publish postmortem, and create follow-ups for long-term fixes
comments: 2025-02-12 10:22 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after support escalated for tenant 'Acme Finance' experiencing hallucination spikes in canary. Initial scope includes automation for KV reconciliation and a bridge pattern for Private tenants.

2025-02-14 09:33 - Liam Nguyen: Spike investigation: observed 3% increase in hallucination score and 2x latency p95 for sequences >1024. Root cause likely KV cache mismatch combined with an auto-quantization kernel change. Adding rehydrate sweep as first mitigation.
2025-02-18 15:02 - Maria Gomez (Support): Reviewed customer communication templates. Requested an extra status field for 'data residency impact' and a simplified blurb for CSMs.
2025-02-21 11:47 - Priya Reddy (Security): Security review scheduled. Bridge prototype must use mutual TLS and short-lived tokens. Approved wire protocol with SRV-Auth token flow.
2025-02-26 08:20 - Liam Nguyen: Prototype of rehydrate-sweep script checked in (PR #8342). Dry-run on staging completed for 5 tenants; average reconciliation time 7.2 minutes for 5000 missing keys.

2025-03-01 17:55 - SRE Oncall (Ben Carter): Performed a staged dry-run with Private bridge in eu-west-1. Observed an edge condition where background cache eviction clashed with rehydrate; added 'lock-kv-keys' step to runbook to prevent evictions during sweep.
2025-03-03 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include end-to-end dry run and documented rollback handshake. Preparing stakeholder review next week.
notes: Trade-offs: Full tenant re-ingestion is more robust but expensive and slow; rehydrate-sweep trades speed for potential residual cache variance. We must track false-negative rates after sweeps.
Open questions: Should bridge service be a lightweight CLI or a long-running agent? Current prototype is a short-lived connector to minimize attack surface.
Mitigation templates: Provide both technical and non-technical customer messages. Technical template includes repro prompts and timestamps for observability teams.
Metrics to add: Add 'rehydrate-success-rate' and 'bridge-handshake-latency' to per-tenant telemetry for future automated decisioning.
Follow-ups: Automate lock-and-sweep as part of the runtime's maintenance window tooling; plan a demo with Solutions Engineering and top-20 customers.
